Procurement startup Fragment is exiting stealth with $56 million raised, CEO Pranav Mulgund tells Axios Pro exclusively.

Why it matters: Tariff changes and supply chain disruptions are making direct procurement even more difficult for manufacturers.

Zoom in: 8VC led the Series A portion, while General Catalyst and A* co-led the seed round. Roelof Botha, former head of Sequoia, is also an investor.

How it works: Fragment says its AI agents and Autonomous Context Engine work across the disparate data systems manufacturers use and tries to resolve purchasing and payment issues.

The San Francisco-based startup, founded in 2025, is selling to dozens of Fortune 1000 customers.

What's next: Fragment is focused on direct procurement for now, but its context engine could be used for other enterprise workflows, Mulgund says.

Follow the money: If the company hits its "aggressive" 2027 revenue goals, it could look for new funding.
